findings.title: Client mutation does not surface errors as ApiError and fails on 204
findings.rationale: Rule 3: client requests must surface errors as `ApiError`. The new `useDismissAllSuggestions` mutation calls `fetch` directly and on any response (including non-2xx) calls `res.json()`. The server returns 204 with no body, so `res.json()` throws a SyntaxError, causing the mutation to fail with a plain `Error` instead of an `ApiError`. On error responses, the code does not check `res.ok` and returns the error body as data, which the `onSuccess` handler then treats as success. This breaks the expected error-handling pattern and will show the user a generic error message.

findings.title: Client mutation calls `res.json()` on a 204 No Content response, which always throws
findings.rationale: The server returns HTTP 204 with no body. `res.json()` on an empty body throws a `SyntaxError` because there is no JSON to parse. This means every successful call to the new endpoint will throw, the mutation will fail, and the button will never work. The caller (the FindingsPanel button) breaks immediately.

findings.title: Client mutation does not surface errors as ApiError and breaks on 204 success
findings.rationale: The new `useDismissAllSuggestions` mutation calls `fetch` directly and unconditionally calls `res.json()`. On a non-2xx response (e.g. 422, 500) it returns the error body as data, so the mutation resolves successfully and `onSuccess` invalidates queries as if the action succeeded. On the expected 204 success, `res.json()` throws a `SyntaxError` because the body is empty, causing the mutation to reject with a plain `Error` instead of an `ApiError`. Both cases violate the project rule that client requests must surface errors as `ApiError` (see `client/src/lib/api.ts:44-58`).

findings.title: Client mutation uses raw fetch and breaks on 204 and non-2xx responses
findings.rationale: The new `useDismissAllSuggestions` mutation calls `fetch` directly and unconditionally returns `res.json()`. The server returns 204 No Content (no body), so `res.json()` throws a syntax error on success, causing the mutation to fail and the UI to show an error. On a non-2xx response, the error body is parsed but not thrown as `ApiError`, so the user sees a generic message and the query invalidation in `onSuccess` still runs, corrupting the cache. This breaks the web client (FindingsPanel) for every caller.

matched_title: Client calls res.json() on 204 No Content response, causing runtime error

findings.title: Client calls res.json() on 204 No Content response, causing runtime error
findings.rationale: The server returns HTTP 204 with no body. The client's `mutationFn` calls `res.json()` unconditionally, which will throw a `SyntaxError` because the response body is empty. This breaks the entire dismiss-all-suggestions feature on every successful call. The caller is the web client. Compatible alternative: either change the server to return an empty JSON object `{}` with status 200, or change the client to check `res.ok` and handle 204 by returning `null` (e.g., `if (res.status === 204) return null;`).

findings.title: Client does not throw ApiError on non-2xx responses
findings.rationale: The client uses `fetch` directly and does not check `res.ok` before calling `res.json()`. On error responses (e.g., 404, 500), `res.json()` will parse the error body (which is JSON with `{ error: { code, message, details } }`) and return it as the mutation result, treating a failure as success. This violates rule 3 (client requests must surface errors as `ApiError`). The fix is to add `if (!res.ok) { /* read error body and throw ApiError */ }` before parsing.

findings.title: Shared contract change not mirrored in client copy
findings.rationale: Rule 2: A shared contract change must be applied to both copies (`server/src/vendor/shared/` and `client/src/vendor/shared/`). This diff only edits the server copy. The client copy will silently diverge, meaning the client's type for `PrMeta` will lack `merge_conflict` until someone manually syncs it. This does not break any caller today (the field is nullish and not read by the client yet), but it creates a maintenance debt and a future mismatch if the client later tries to use the field.
